findings.summary: Ambient, pinned, and governed webgpu@0.3.10 each fail three Electron main-process executions because the native addon requests an external ArrayBuffer prohibited by this Node-API host.

Clean-installed Doe executes the unchanged tropical-SpMV application in three Electron main processes and exact replay; all four output hashes equal their independent CPU oracle hashes on the physical Radeon Vulkan adapter.

A source-built node-webgpu and Dawn control with a frozen two-file owned-ArrayBuffer fallback also passes three exact processes and replay. The bounded incumbent correction closes the application gap, so DoeRuntime ownership is rejected for this tuple.

limitations: The Electron lane is main-process Node-side compute and creates no renderer.
Three clean processes per passing lane remain below the promotion reliability floor.
The P0 control is a pinned source build, not a claim-eligible clean application installation.
Process-tree RSS values are five-millisecond Linux procfs diagnostic peaks, not memory-growth or leak evidence.
No selected-operation performance comparison was run.
The result grants no application promotion, release, Chromium, browser, or external-adoption credit.

performance.reason: The diagnostic adjudicates exact compatibility and correction ownership, not selected-operation performance.

receiptOverhead.reason: Electron process durations were not admitted as a receipt-overhead comparison.

I0.summary: Ambient webgpu@0.3.10 fails at the external-ArrayBuffer boundary in all three processes.

I1.summary: The explicitly pinned incumbent fails at the same native boundary in all three processes.

W0.summary: DoeProof makes the incumbent failure explicit but cannot correct it above the native addon.

D0.summary: Doe passes the exact application oracle in three processes and replay.

P0.summary: The source-built bounded incumbent patch passes the same exact application oracle in three processes and replay.

materialOutcome.summary: D0 does not provide an application outcome unavailable from the smaller P0 correction.

costAcceptance.summary: The bounded upstream correction carries less durable compatibility and support obligation than owning DoeRuntime for this tuple.

installation.summary: Doe is clean-installed, but P0 is a controlled source build rather than a promoted application installation.

supportHardware.summary: Both passing lanes bind the physical Radeon Vulkan adapter without software fallback.

teardown.summary: Processes exit, but promotion-scale teardown and device-loss injection were not run.

memory.summary: Diagnostic process-tree peaks were observed, but bounded-growth testing was not run.

receipts.summary: The complete diagnostic, plan, implementation, patch, package, toolchain, and application inputs are hash-bound.

replay.summary: Doe and P0 each reproduce their exact semantic application evidence.

performance.summary: No predeclared selected-operation performance result exists.

ownership.summary: P0 closes the same application gap as D0 with a smaller durable ownership surface.

release.summary: HoloScript Electron remains a diagnostic regression, not a release dependency.
